text:
**For a full recharge from empty in one sunny day, plan on about 300-350 W of panels. A 200 W panel does it in about 1.5 days.**

**The formula** (panel watts × peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75 real-world efficiency = Wh per day):
- At 4 peak sun hours, a one-day recharge takes about 340 W of panels ([Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)).
- At 5 peak sun hours, it takes about 270 W ([Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)).
- In a good summer, it takes about 300 W ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).
- In a northern winter (about 2 sun hours), it takes about 700 W or more ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

**By panel size** (4.5 sun hours, 70% efficiency, per [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)):
- 100 W: about 315 Wh/day, so roughly 3 days.
- 200 W: about 630 Wh/day, so roughly 1.5 days.
- 400 W: about 1,260 Wh/day, so under a day.

A quick rule of thumb is battery Wh ÷ 5, which gives about 200 W for a day and a half of decent sun ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).

**Before you buy, check:**
- **Solar input limit:** Panels beyond your station's maximum solar input add nothing. Many 1,000 Wh units accept 400-800 W, but some cap at 200 W ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).
- **Voltage:** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside the station's input range, or you risk damaging the charge controller. Be extra careful when wiring panels in series ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **Loads:** If you're running devices while charging, subtract that draw from the solar input, which slows the recharge.

**One option if you want a 400 W panel:** the [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W Foldable Solar Panel](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel). The page lists it at $299, or $269.10 with code ALLPOWERS26 (expires 2026-12-30). It has 45.3 V Voc and MC4-style connectors with adapters, and it weighs 18.5 kg. It's too high-voltage for stations with a 24-28 V max input, and the page notes it works with 12-60 V inputs. The site earns a commission on purchases, and checkout has the final word on price.
